question: When the endpoint refuses mid-run — a 429 on a free OpenRouter model, a 5xx, a context-length error — what does the loop do?

options.label: Retry 429/5xx a few times, then fail
options.reason: Free OpenRouter models rate-limit often and briefly. A short backoff (3 tries) turns most of those into a finished run instead of a failed one. Anything else — 400, 401, context length — fails at once with the status in the reason.
options.costLater: A run can sit silent for the backoff window; the log has to say 'waiting on 429, try 2 of 3' or it looks stuck (the `pcsz` node's rule). The bound is a number somebody will want to tune.

options.label: Fail at once, name the status
options.reason: Smallest loop. The run ends `failed` with the HTTP status and the body's message; the `backup-8erx` node is where a second model gets tried.
options.costLater: On free models a large share of runs fail on the first 429 and the human re-runs by hand until the backup node lands. Every retry is a full worktree prepare.

options.label: Fall through to the next model in `dispatch.models`
options.reason: The loop itself picks the next covering entry on 429/5xx, so a free model's limit never costs a run.
options.costLater: Model choice leaks out of Jev and `dispatch.ts` into the loop, and the run record's model field is no longer what Jev picked. Overlaps the `backup-8erx` node; two mechanisms for one fallback.
